stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist has completed no training programme of any kind. She proposes to dispense emergency contraception under the statewide standing order this week, and to dispense a COVID-19 drug under a standing order next week. How do the two proposals compare?

choices.text: The emergency contraception dispensing may proceed; the COVID-19 drug may not.
The COVID-19 dispensing may proceed; the emergency contraception may not.
Both may proceed, because training is a professional expectation rather than a bar.
Neither may proceed, because both regimes require approved training beforehand.
Both may proceed once she notifies the Department that she intends to dispense.

explanation.core_reasoning: M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 19A(d) provides that before dispensing emergency contraception a pharmacist MAY complete a Commissioner-approved training programme. M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 19E(c) provides that before dispensing a COVID-19 drug a pharmacist SHALL complete such a programme. The two adjacent standing-order regimes differ on exactly this point.

choice_analysis.A: Correct: permissive in one regime and mandatory in the other.
choice_analysis.C: The COVID-19 training is a statutory precondition.
choice_analysis.D: The emergency contraception training is permissive.
choice_analysis.E: Notification to the Department is not the precondition in issue.

related_facts: The COVID-19 training must cover review of recent laboratory blood work
explanation.mpje_trap: Candidates assume one uniform training rule governs every statewide standing order.

reasoning_steps: Identify which standing-order regime each proposal engages
Read the training provision belonging to each regime
Note that one says may and the other says shall
